target: Она искала ключи и наконец нашла их.
english: She was looking for keys and finally found them.
tip: искала then нашла (iskala, nashla): the imperfective describes the process of searching, and the perfective marks the successful result of finding.

target: Он решал задачу час и решил её.
english: He was solving the problem for an hour and solved it.
tip: решал then решил (reshal, reshil): the imperfective form shows the hour-long effort, and the perfective form marks the moment it finally got solved.

english: The professor delivers a lecture on physics.
tip: To say about X, use о (o = about) plus the noun in -е (-e): о физике (o fizike = about physics). Before a vowel it becomes об (ob), as in об отце (ob ottse = about dad).

english: What is the weather like today?
tip: Weather questions use какая (kakaya = what kind), agreeing with feminine погода (pogoda = weather), where English just says how.

english: We usually wrote the paper.
tip: обычно (obychno = usually) takes the imperfective писали (pisali = wrote), stressing a repeated habit, not one finished paper.

english: He immediately wrote the paper.
tip: сразу (srazu = at once) marks a finished action, so the perfective написал (napisal = wrote) is used, not the process form писал (pisal).

english: We finally did the exercise.
tip: наконец (nakonets = finally) points to a result, so the perfective сделали (sdelali = did) is used, not the ongoing делали (delali).

english: She often built the lesson.
tip: Past verbs agree with the subject's gender: feminine она (ona) takes строила (stroila = built) with -ла, while a man would say строил (stroil).

english: She often answered the letter.
tip: отвечать (otvechat = to answer) pairs with на (na) plus the accusative: отвечала на письмо (otvechala na pismo = answered the letter).

english: She quickly forgot about it.
tip: забыть (zabyt = to forget) takes о (o) about something, which becomes об (ob) before a vowel: забыла об этом (zabyla ob etom = forgot about it).

english: She left her friend's place.
tip: Leaving a person uses от (ot = from) plus the genitive: ушла от подруги (ushla ot podrugi = left her friend).

english: Why is it so cold here?
tip: Cold has no subject here: холодно (kholodno = cold) is an adverb form used for weather and how a place feels.

english: I will need an umbrella today.
tip: Needing something puts the person in the dative: мне (mne = to me) plus понадобится (ponadobitsya = will be needed), literally to-me it will be needed.

english: He was writing the paper all day.
tip: весь день (ves den = all day) describes duration, so the imperfective писал (pisal = was writing) is used, not the finished написал (napisal).

english: One time is enough to understand.
tip: чтобы (chtoby = in order to) plus an infinitive shows purpose: чтобы понять (chtoby ponyat = in order to understand).

english: I often went to the market.
tip: Repeated round trips use the multidirectional ходила (khodila = went), not the one-way шла (shla), so часто ходила (chasto khodila) means going there again and again.

english: It's a fifteen-minute walk to the station.
tip: After numbers from five up, the noun goes to genitive plural: пятнадцать минут (pyatnadtsat minut = fifteen minutes), not минуты (minuty).

english: We need to go to the doctor.
tip: Going to a person uses к (k = to) plus the dative: к врачу (k vrachu = to the doctor), where places take в (v) or на (na).

english: I gave the book to my brother.
tip: The receiver of дал (dal = gave) stands in the dative: своему брату (svoemu bratu = to my brother).

target: Дедушка играет в шахматы после обеда.
english: Grandfather plays chess after lunch.
tip: Playing a game uses играть (igrat) plus в (v) and the accusative: играет в шахматы (igrayet v shakhmaty = plays chess).

target: Мы плавали в море каждое утро.
english: We swam in the sea every morning.
tip: каждое утро (kazhdoye utro = every morning) signals a habit, so the multidirectional плавали (plavali = swam) fits regular swims.

target: Дети бегали во дворе весь день.
english: The children ran around the yard all day.
tip: бегали (begali = ran around) is the multidirectional form for running in all directions, not toward one goal like бегут (begut).

target: Сколько бы он ни работал, денег не хватает.
english: No matter how much he works, the money isn't enough.
tip: Сколько бы он ни (skolko by on ni = no matter how much) makes a concession: however much he works, it is never enough.

target: Если бы мы знали дорогу, мы бы не опоздали.
english: If we had known the way, we wouldn't have been late.
tip: Unreal past uses если бы (esli by = if) with a past verb, then бы again: мы бы не опоздали (my by ne opozdali = we would not have been late).

english: Tomorrow the salesman will wash the dishes.
tip: A perfective in present form means future: помоет (pomoyet = will wash) refers to tomorrow, with no separate will word.

english: The musician always helps a friend.
tip: помогать (pomogat = to help) governs the dative, not the accusative: помогает другу (pomogayet drugu = helps a friend).

english: The boy constantly lost toys.
tip: Repeated losing uses the imperfective терял (teryal = lost): постоянно терял (postoyanno teryal) marks it happening over and over.

english: The boy lost his favorite toy.
tip: A single completed loss uses the perfective потерял (poteryal = lost), formed by adding по- to терял (teryal).

english: The children are running to the playground.
tip: Motion toward one goal uses the unidirectional бегут (begut = are running): бегут на площадку (begut na ploshchadku = running to the playground) means heading there now.

english: My mom makes the best borscht.
tip: лучший (luchshiy = best) is the irregular superlative of good, standing in for a regular form like самый хороший (samyy khoroshiy).
